input.objective: Launch PLEA test run 3 on Sepolia from this Foundry repository exactly as launch.json lists it: seven contracts (PLEA, CabalGate, Seasons, Laureates, PleaDistributor, Letterbox, PleaLaunch), deployed in order in one transaction with the constructor arguments in launch.json. This is the code of launch #1311 (your accepted run-2 adaptation and its audit fixes kept) plus five changes. (1) Letters and auto-sell: a new ownerless Letterbox. Anyone pleads by sending a transaction whose input data is the plea text (fallback), or by calling letter(text) with the same text from a block explorer's Write Contract tab; commands APPEAL, SELL and NAME; a letter pleads a fixed 10% of the writer's PLEA, held in escrow. The oracle fee, a 0.25 IMD runner tip and an appeal's 0.35 IMD wall share are paid in the same transaction by the gate selling the writer's PLEA for exactly that IMD (exact-output swap through the hook, at most the hourly snapshot value plus 10%; on Sepolia the Letterbox mints the 0.5 test oracle fee instead, a constructor flag refused on chain id 1). Anyone sells an approved escrowed plea with deliver for at least 95% of its snapshot value and earns the tip; settle returns the escrow and the tip on every other ending; status and leaderboard are text views. No Letterbox function ID can be the start of valid UTF-8 text (a test checks the ABI). CabalGate gains submitFor, appealFor and executeSellFor that only the Letterbox may call, plea flags with a PleaFlags event, and lastPleaOf; its own executeSell refuses escrowed pleas. PLEA gains setLetterbox (launcher only, once, from PleaLaunch's constructor) and courtTake (Letterbox only, moving the caller's own PLEA into escrow); the Letterbox is an exempt sender. Laureates gains setNameFor (Letterbox only) and a By letter seal. (2) A plea is at least 1% of the seller's balance, or 2.5M PLEA when that is less. (3) The PLEA owner does not play: no season points, IMD prize, PLEA bonus, Laureate or rebalance keeper tip. (4) A six-season PLEA bonus: PLEA.init mints 87% to the hook, 3% to Seasons and 10% to the distributor; each of the first six seasons pays 5,000,000 PLEA to its qualifying top 10 and burns the unpaid rest; flushToWall burns what is left; nobody can withdraw it. (5) The Cabal's judging rules version 2 in CabalGate.DEFINITIONS (plea, stories, content, manipulation, answer), calibrated with live Sepolia panels: keep the text exactly. (6) A gas pass that changes no behaviour: the oracle body JSON-escapes only the plea texts (byte-identical to escaping the whole question), the text rules read bytes without bounds checks, PleaHook.latestPrice and price24hAgo read one checkpoint and scan the ring only as a fallback, and a Letterbox escrow fits one slot; test/GasPass.t.sol holds each to the code it replaced. Audit the imported code and deploy it unchanged; fix only what the audit proves is a real bug, and keep every number as it is (fees, timings, panel 30, quorum 17, 5-hour seasons, 33-hour dead-man, START 1792162800, credit gas 1300000, letters 10%, tip 0.25 IMD, 95% sale minimum, fee cap +10%, 1% plea minimum, six bonus seasons of 5,000,000 PLEA, the 87/3/10 split). CabalGate's runtime is 24,292 bytes, 284 under the EIP-170 limit: keep any fix within it. On Sepolia the seven-contract deploy exceeds 16,777,216 gas (about 24.6M; launch #1242 used 81.8M in one transaction); the manifest test reports that margin instead of asserting it. PleaHook is not a launch.json entry: PleaLaunch.deployHook deploys it after launch with a salt mined off chain. Keep PLEA.setLauncher accepting either the deploy-transaction flag or PLEA's deployment block. Keep foundry.toml as it is, including [lint] lint_on_build = false and the read-only fs_permissions for ./out (the Letterbox ABI test).
